narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

A high of 29°C (84°F) is expected today with mostly cloudy skies early through midday, becoming overcast by evening. Isolated Evening Showers & Thunderstorms are expected from 18:00, delivering 4.4 mm (0.17 in) of rain, with thunder possible from the morning, peaking this evening. Winds will be north-northeasterly overnight, turning southwest by midday, with peak gusts reaching 42 km/h (23 kt) ashore. The UV index will peak at 8.8. Air quality is expected at AQI 75. Overnight, temperatures will drop to a low of 19°C (66°F). As of 06:01, reports through 05:00: no rain; no thunder; high so far 20°C (68°F); low so far 20°C (68°F); peak sustained 9 km/h (5 kt); sky mostly cloudy.

## Extended Outlook

temperatures and winds much the same through Wednesday, with showers and thunderstorms likely each day. Monday will be mostly cloudy with four of four models wet and thunder likely, reaching 27–30°C (81–86°F). Tuesday brings mostly cloudy skies with three of four models wet and thunder likely. Wednesday is overcast with four of four models wet, thunder likely, and a 100% rain call, with highs of 25–29°C (77–84°F). Thursday stays overcast with four of four models wet and thunder possible, with highs of 24–26°C (75–79°F). Friday remains overcast with four of four models wet and thunder possible, reaching 18–25°C (64–77°F). Saturday brings mostly cloudy skies with three of three models wet and thunder possible. Sunday is mostly cloudy with two of two models wet, thunder possible, and a 100% rain call, reaching 26–28°C (79–82°F).

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Thunderstorms are expected ahead, with peak CAPE reaching 1250 J/kg in GFS, 2220 J/kg in ECMWF and Best Match, 1770 J/kg in ICON, and 3540 J/kg in UKMO, all peaking at 19:00. Any thunderstorm brings the hazard of sudden gusts well above the forecast wind.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

On the Winam Gulf, winds will be northeasterly overnight at 6 km/h (3 kt) gusting 8 km/h (4 kt), then south-southwesterly by midday at 9 km/h (5 kt) gusting 22 km/h (12 kt), then into the evening at 13 km/h (7 kt) gusting 22 km/h (12 kt); peak gust 34 km/h (18 kt). Thunderstorms bring the hazard of sudden gusts well above the forecast wind.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1011 hPa) and highest toward the northeast (1014 hPa) — a 4 hPa spread, a weak large-scale gradient. Pressure overhead is near-steady. Sampling is a nine-point ring at 12-degree spacing, so this locates a direction, not a centre or a front. Across 5 points, today's mean sea-level pressure sits between 1015.2 and 1017.0 hPa; near-steady over three days (-0.1 hPa). The pressure trend is +1.7 hPa, with a weak large-scale gradient and lowest pressure toward the north.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

At Day+0, no model is meaningfully better than the others overall, though GFS holds the best rain record at 90%. Today's high call of 29°C (84°F) aligns with the Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) forecast of 29°C (84°F) max and 18°C (64°F) min, which also expects light showers and thunderstorms. Against models today, GFS forecasts a higher high at 30.2°C (86.4°F), sitting on the higher side consistent with review findings that GFS over-forecasts daytime highs. ECMWF forecasts 27.7°C (81.9°F), ICON 28.7°C (83.7°F), UKMO 29.7°C (85.5°F), and Best Match 27.9°C (82.2°F). Best Match projects gusts to 50.4 km/h (27 kt). At Day+7, ECMWF is the strongest rain caller and GFS the weakest. Data sufficiency is settled at Day+0 with 66 checks, while Day+3 has 27 checks and Day+7 has 81 checks per model. Best Match rain probability mirrors ECMWF.

extended_outlook:
Temperatures and winds much the same through Wednesday, with rain and thunderstorms likely each day. Skies mostly cloudy Monday and Tuesday, then overcast Wednesday. Wednesday's call: rain, 100%, with all four models wet; highs 25 to 29°C (78 to 84°F). Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) calls it wet. At this lead Best Match has the best record, right 90% of the time over 85 checks.

Further out, temperatures and winds much the same through Sunday, with rain and thunderstorms possible each day. Thursday: all four models wet, the week's wettest day at 17 mm (0.67 in) on average, highs around 25°C (77°F), thunder possible rather than likely. Friday: all four models wet, highs 18 to 25°C (65 to 77°F). Saturday: all three models that reach it wet, highs around 26°C (79°F).

Only GFS, ECMWF and ICON reach past Friday. UKMO is the wetter solution from Thursday to Friday; GFS, ECMWF and ICON keep it drier. Sunday's call: rain, 100%, with both models wet; highs around 27°C (81°F). At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 90% of the time over 81 checks.
